findings.body: The branch still adds a new interactive disclosure without evidence of the required impeccable shape/audit/polish pass or a specifically tasked emil-design-eng interaction review. The updated browser walk checks keyboard, touch, focus, and sizing, but it does not claim either required design pass or cover the full visual and interaction checklist, including press feedback and state/copy polish.

findings.body: The component test still injects a completed `rowLabels` response through the mocked Ask API. The updated functional check likewise says it manually attached resolver output in the browser because the production chat service does not emit it yet. Thus there is no running-API/real-database/browser proof that production carries resolved labels into this table; the task plan assigns that wiring and crossing proof to GL-ANSWER-WIRING.
findings.title: Later: prove labels through the running Ask stack → GL-ANSWER-WIRING

findings.body: The batching change reduces network round trips, but it builds each batch by UNIONing one `nameSelect` per row, and every arm independently scans `sap_transaction` once for the scoped count and again for name groups. With the default limits, a valid 1,000-row answer still performs 2,000 scoped scans, with 100 scans packed into each timeout-bounded query. Supported GL answers share their batch/window/plant scope and differ principally by GL code, so they can be resolved set-wise in a single grouped scan per batch.
findings.title: Batch resolver still scans transactions twice per answer row
